name: Citizenship by Marriage (Foreign Wife of an Egyptian Man)

qualifying_event.description: A foreign woman who marries an Egyptian man may acquire Egyptian nationality after formally notifying the Ministry of Interior, provided the marriage subsists for 2 years from the date of notification.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage certificate; formal notification to the Ministry of Interior.

requirements.blocker_text: Available to a foreign WOMAN who marries an Egyptian man (Article 7). No equivalent provision was found in the primary law for a foreign man marrying an Egyptian woman -- Article 12 instead confirms an Egyptian woman marrying a foreigner retains her own Egyptian nationality, but does not grant her husband Egyptian nationality.
Marriage must subsist for 2 years from the date of formal notification to the Ministry of Interior, unless the marriage ends due to the husband's death.
requirements.fix_path: Submit notification and remain married for 2 years from that date.

evidence_required.document: Formal notification to the Ministry of Interior

sources.title: Egypt -- Law No. 26 of 1975 Concerning Egyptian Nationality (official English translation), Article 7: foreign wife of an Egyptian man may acquire nationality after 2 years from notification; Article 12: Egyptian women retain their own nationality upon marrying a foreigner, with no reciprocal grant to the foreign husband

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Egypt). A genuinely gender-restricted marriage route, comparable to the pattern flagged for the UAE and Bahamas elsewhere in this dataset: the law provides a marriage-based citizenship route ONLY for a foreign woman marrying an Egyptian man. A foreign man marrying an Egyptian woman has NO equivalent marriage-based path under the text located in this pass -- he would need to rely on ordinary naturalization (see eg_naturalisation.json) like any other unrelated foreign resident, typically the far longer 10-year standard route. This asymmetry is sourced to the ORIGINAL 1975 text; it was not independently confirmed whether Law 154/2004 or any later amendment altered Article 7 or Article 12 specifically (that amendment's confirmed changes, per secondary sourcing, targeted descent/maternal-transmission provisions -- see eg_citizenship_by_descent.json -- not the marriage article), so this reflects the best-available primary-text reading rather than a fully current-verified one.
